name: present tense
title: Spanish Present Tense Practice: Regular -ar, -er, -ir Verbs Quiz
description: Practice the Spanish present tense: regular -ar, -er and -ir endings, common irregular verbs and uses, with a rule table and 10 sentences checked as you tap.
answer: The Spanish present tense drops -ar, -er or -ir and adds endings for each person: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, hablan; como, comes, come, comemos, comen; vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, viven. It covers what you do usually, what is happening now and fixed plans in the near future.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127b.csv

rules.use: Near future with a time word

quiz.after: en un restaurante los fines de semana.
en la cafetería a las doce.
quiz.why: No stem change with nosotros: almorzamos.
Hacer is irregular in yo: hago.
Ustedes takes the ellos form: escriben.
Empezar changes e to ie: empieza.

quiz.after: a Miami; el vuelo sale a las ocho.
quiz.why: A fixed plan with a time word can take the present.

mistakes: Using the infinitive after a subject: «yo hablar español» should be «yo hablo español».
Adding estar for every present action: «estoy trabajo» is wrong; say «trabajo» or «estoy trabajando».
Forgetting irregular yo forms: «yo hacio» should be «yo hago», «yo teno» should be «yo tengo».
Applying the stem change to nosotros: «queremos», not «quieremos».
Using -an endings for -er and -ir verbs: «ellos coman» is subjunctive; the present is «ellos comen».

heritage: Heritage speakers usually conjugate the present without thinking. In writing, look at the irregular yo forms that some families pronounce differently (haiga for haya is a separate issue) and at accents on words around the verb, like qué and cuándo in questions: ¿Qué haces?
teacher: Students write five sentences about their week, one with each person (yo, tú, él, nosotros, ellos). Partners correct only the endings, then each reads the best sentence aloud.

faq.question: How many endings does the present tense have?
faq.answer: Five you will use all the time: yo, tú, él/ella/usted, nosotros and ellos/ellas/ustedes. Vosotros (Spain) adds a sixth form, which most US courses teach for recognition only.

faq.question: Can the Spanish present mean the future?
faq.answer: Yes, with a time word and a fixed plan: mañana trabajo, el lunes empiezo. For less fixed plans, Spanish uses ir a + infinitive: voy a trabajar.

faq.question: What are the most common irregular verbs?
faq.answer: Ser, estar, ir, tener, hacer, decir, poder, querer and venir. Many verbs are irregular only in yo: tengo, hago, pongo, salgo, conozco, traigo.
